outOfScopeButFlagged: PostgresTaskStore.recordCompletionSummary passes {id: taskId} into insertCompletionSummary — the id column ends up being the task id, not the summary's UUID. Latent; affects any reconciler that compares per-record UUIDs. (lib/postgres-store.mjs:445)

PostgresTaskStore.recordAuditReview inserts the audit row first, then conditionally calls updateTask outside the original withClient transaction. If the updateTask transaction fails after the audit row committed, you end up with verdict:'pending' but task still in 'completed'. (lib/postgres-store.mjs:401-426)

TaskStore.searchPlanningMemory and PostgresTaskStore.searchPlanningMemory use different algorithms (JSON.stringify includes vs SQL LIKE on lower(...)); they will return different results on identical inputs. (lib/store.ts:516 vs lib/postgres-store.ts:499-513)
ownerDecisionsRequired: AXI_TODO_STORE default 'postgres' → 'json' is a breaking change for anyone depending on the current default. M2 does NOT flip it. README contains the export AXI_TODO_STORE=json recipe; owner owns the swap commit when ready.
Whether to delete the PG schema / bin/axi-todo-migrate-postgres.mjs after consolidation, or keep them as opt-in for environments that prefer PG durability. M2 keeps both intact.

The 18 pre-existing JSON entries that already have status='completed' (from before M1's completion gate landed) were not auto-promoted to 'awaiting_audit' per the M1 commit directive. A separate owner-driven recheck task should decide whether to re-evaluate them. See M2.S7 evidence.
newFindings: PostgreSQL store schema does not store its own provenance field; the importer relies on the PG `id` text PK and the `payload` jsonb round-trip. If a future tool mutates PG `payload` to drop fields, the JSON round-trip will lose them. Consider adding a `source` text column to PG schema (migration not in M2 scope).

warnIfDualPopulated reads BOTH stores on every startup; for an empty other-store the JSON read is cheap (single fs.readFile), but the PG read opens a real connection. For daemons that boot repeatedly this could add startup latency. M2 does not optimise; consider a 'probe once and cache' option if it becomes a real issue.
